paper_title: Dynamic Set Cover with Worst-Case Recourse
classifications: Theory of computation → Dynamic graph algorithms
statement: This leaves the following open question. Is there an alternative approach – possibly abandoning the black-box paradigm – that avoids limitations (1) and (2)? In particular, can one reduce or eliminate the factor-2 loss in the approximation guarantee and/or achieve a sublinear, preferably polylogarithmic, dependence on the aspect ratio C? We view these as the main directions for future work.
context: Our black-box transformation relies on the reconfiguration problem. As discussed in Section 2.1, even for vertex cover this framework inherently incurs the approximation blow-up in (1), as well as the recourse dependencies in (2) and (3). This leaves the following open question. Is there an alternative approach – possibly abandoning the black-box paradigm – that avoids limitations (1) and (2)? In particular, can one reduce or eliminate the factor-2 loss in the approximation guarantee and/or achieve a sublinear, preferably polylogarithmic, dependence on the aspect ratio C? We view these as the main directions for future work.
